JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 12.06.2018 in M.V.C.No.25/2016 passed by the Addl. District Judge and Addl. M.A.C.T., Udupi (Sitting at Kundapura) ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 18.12.2014 at about 01:00 pm, the petitioner was travelling in a tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-19/B-6833 as a Cleaner, near Ettaki Village of Hosanagara Taluk,
sustained the injuries due to capsize of the tipper.
After taking treatment at Sri. Jayachamarajendra General Hospital, Theerthahalli and K.M.C. Hospital, Manipal, he has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.9,10,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after NC: 2023:KHC:45765 taking the evidence, awarded compensation of Rs.2,18,740/-
with 6% interest p.a., fastening the liability against the owner of the tipper.

Aggrieved by the same,
the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. S.M. Anfel, learned counsel on behalf of Sri. K. Prasanna Shetty,
learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. S.V. Hegde Mulkhand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries over his right eyebrow, fracture of pelvis, blunt injury to the abdomen with grade-IV lever laceration, fracture of right zygomatic bone and he was under hospitalization.
In spite of producing medical evidence explaining that the petitioner has suffered 9% whole body disability, the Tribunal has assessed it at 4.5%.

The Tribunal has not awarded NC: 2023:KHC:45765 compensation under different heads; fastening the liability against the owner is erroneous as on the date of accident, the driver of the tipper was holding valid driving licence to drive light motor vehicle, but his heavy goods vehicle driving licence was valid till 27.04.2014, renewed on 06.18.2015.
Hence, the Insurance Company has to pay the compensation and he sought for interference.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the driver of the tipper did not hold valid driving licence on 18.12.2014, the date of accident.
A notice was issued to the owner of the vehicle to produce the driving licence, but he has not produced the same.
On behalf of the Insurance Company, Sri. Ramakrishna Rai, A.R.T.O., Udupi has been examined as RW-2, he has clearly stated that the driver was not holding driving licence on the date of accident.
For this reason, the Tribunal has fastened the liability against the owner.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the medical evidence did point out whole body disability of 4.5% and therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed it and determined the loss of future earnings.
Hence, the finding recorded by the Tribunal is perfect and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
To explain the injuries and disability, PW-2 Dr. Kiran Acharya, Professor of Orthopedics, K.M.C. Hospital, Manipal has given evidence before the Tribunal.

His evidence points out various injuries sustained by the petitioner, particularly 2 fractures such as pelvis and right zygomatic fracture, laceration over right eyebrow, blunt injury to the abdomen with liver laceration NC: 2023:KHC:45765 Grade IV.
Doctor is of the opinion that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of 9% of locomotor functions of the body.
The cross-examination of the Medical Officer did not demonstrate anything that the 9% assessed is a limb disability.
Contrary in the cross-examination, the Doctor has reiterated 9% is the whole body disability.
Therefore, the disability assessed on the basis of the nature of the injuries and veracity of the medical evidence, it is fairly accepted that the petitioner has sustained 9% whole body disability.
9. The petitioner is admittedly, the Cleaner of the lorry.
He has no proof of income.
The Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.9,000/- which could be quite reasonable for the year 2014 and there is no need to interfere in it.

10. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation as follows:
NC: 2023:KHC:45765 Sl. No. Particulars Rs.

Injury, pain and sufferings 40,000 2 Medical expenses 43,358 3 Loss of earning during 3,900 treatment 4 Loss of bed rest 36,000 5 Loss of future earning capacity 87,480 6 Conveyance, nourishment and 8,000 attendant charges Total 2,18,738 10.1.
Having regard to the nature of injuries, the Tribunal has committed error in not awarding loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence, the compensation towards loss of amenities and discomfort, loss of future earnings and future medical expenses has to be determined.
Compensation awarded under the other heads has to be maintained as it is.
The petitioner has suffered the injuries referred supra.
He was under hospitalization for 14 days and he took follow up NC: 2023:KHC:45765 treatment on 14.01.2015 and 05.03.2015 at the Outpatient Department, K.M.C. Hospital, Manipal.
Hence, he was laid up for not less than 6 months and therefore, loss of income during laid-up has to assessed at Rs.54,000/- as against Rs.39,900/- assessed by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 3 the future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-.
The petitioner was aged 21 years, future prospects of 40% has to be added.

If whole body disability is taken at 9%, loss of future earnings comes to Rs.9,000/- + Rs.3,600/- (40%) = Rs.12,600/- x 12 x '18'
multiplier x 9% = Rs.2,44,944/- as against Rs.87,480/-.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to compensation as hereunder:
 Sl. No. Particulars Rs.
 1 Pain and sufferings 40,000
2 Medical expenses 43,358  3 Loss of income during laid-up for 6 54,000  months  NC: 2023:KHC:45765  4 Food, nourishment and attendant 8,000  charges  5 Loss of amenities and discomfort 40,000
6 Loss of future earnings 2,44,944
7 Future medical expenses 20,000  Total 4,50,302
This is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

11. As regarding liability is concerned, RW-1 A.R.T.O., whose evidence points out that the driver of the tipper was holding a heavy goods vehicle driving licence for a period between 28.04.2011 to 27.04.2014.
The said driving licence was again renewed from 06.08.2015 to 05.08.2018, whereas the accident took place on 18.12.2014.
According to him, on the date of accident, the driver did not hold driving licence to drive heavy good vehicle.
His evidence points out that the driver did posses driving licence to drive light motor vehicle.

sentences.text: In a case of this nature, where there is no valid driving licence, but there is no evidence that the accident occurred on account of non-holding of the driving licence.
Hence, it is a case of breach of conditions of the policy.

12. The Hon'ble Apex court in Singh Ram's case (supra) referring to the driving licence already expired before the accident and was not renewed within prescribed period and it was renewed well (2017) 14 SCC 663 Civil Appeal No.841 of 2018, decided on 08.03.2022 Civil Appeal No.2103 of 2018, arising out of SLP(C) No.22630/2015, decided on 06.03.2018 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:45765 after two years, had held that pay and recovery is proper.
In view of the settled law for breach of conditions, the Insurance Company can avoid its liability, but at the same time, the petitioner cannot be forced to proceed against the owner of the tipper.
The Insurance Company has to deposit the compensation and to recover the same from the owner of the lorry in the very same proceedings.
13. In the light of these, the finding recorded by the Tribunal in exonerating the Insurance Company holding that pay and recovery is not applicable is erroneous.

Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.

iii) The petitioner would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,50,302/-
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:45765 along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, excluding interest for the delayed period of 553 days in filing the appeal and also excluding interest on future medical expenses.

iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and recover the same from owner of the tipper in the very same proceedings.
